items.title: 1. My Brain Feels Damaged: why you trust DMSO, and how far the evidence goes
items.where: If Someone Says "My Brain Feels Damaged": DMSO + Humic Acid + Electrolytes First, P11
items.your_version:
If Someone Says "My Brain Feels Damaged": DMSO + Humic Acid + Electrolytes First

I believe, based on my experience and those of others I've heard from, as well as the books I've read on this, that DMSO works better for most acute brain damage than anything else readily available. The clinical evidence is incomplete, but it leans this way. In animals, when given after a stroke, it shrank the area of the brain that died (which is a good thing). In one human trial, some clot stroke patients seemed to recover better on DMSO, and doctors have used it in a small series of patients to bring down dangerous pressure inside the skull. But more relevant to the drug overdose issue this article deals with, DMSO calms NMDA- and AMPA-mediated excitotoxicity that kills brain cells.

items.my_version: I believe DMSO works better for stroke and most acute brain damage than anything else readily available to ordinary people. That judgment is stronger than the clinical evidence, but the evidence is not empty: a preliminary human ischemic-stroke trial reported possible neurological benefit; a small human series used DMSO for intracranial hypertension; and animal stroke research found substantial infarct reduction even when treatment began after ischemia. DMSO also suppresses NMDA- and AMPA-mediated excitotoxicity.
